overview: Haehyun is a character of extremes. Her damage output is extremely high because she has Shinken (623K~1/4/7, aka Four Tigers Sword Reverse), a high damage, normal-hit launcher that loops into itself. 2H and 6P both combo into Shinken — 2H in particular is very useful since Haehyun can gatling from 2K into 2H, connecting her biggest combo tool from her fastest low. After a Shinken loop, Haehyun can use her 3-hit H Tuning Ball (236H) to set up oppressive okizeme; Tuning Balls can be steered simultaneously with Haehyun once active, letting her combo off her throw, her fast 5H(2) overhead, or various frame traps. If she needs to block, she can rely on her extremely good 2P to mash out of pressure, or use her Enlightened 3000 Palm Strike (236236H) reversal super. However, her neutral and movement are extremely linear compared to most characters: slow walk/run speed and a big hurtbox give her trouble backdashing and evading projectiles/pokes. j.2K and air hayabusa (j.214K) can change her air momentum but don't let her shortcut neutral entirely. Her ground pokes — f.S, 5K, Hayabusa (214K, aka Falcon Dive) — have decent range and size, but few options into or out of them, so she struggles to make her neutral ambiguous and often waits for the opponent's mistake. Her high effective health lets her be patient. Haehyun is slow and straightforward almost to a fault, but has solid defensive options her opponents must respect — if they don't, she can turn a round with a single monstrous combo that sets up equally monstrous okizeme.

pros: Simple neutral: 5K and f.S are straightforward pokes; given space, set up a Tuning Ball. 236236S (Celestial Tuning Ball) often immediately controls neutral once she has 50 meter
Fantastic knockdown game: her okizeme revolves around the controllable Tuning Ball fireball, pulled back toward the opponent after a knockdown for a savage 50/50 with multiple mixup points

'Kick of the Gods': Shinken (623[K]~4 Red) is an incredibly strong move with high base damage and excellent return; a Shinken loop combo deals huge damage and gets great oki, potentially restarting the whole process
Scrapper: great pressure options up close, such as a lightning fast 2P and +3 c.S; high health and huge stun resistance let her take hits and stand strong
Unblockables: multiple unblockables guaranteed with proper setup and ball control
Weird air hurtbox: along with her super heavy weight, some characters struggle to combo her with their basic combos
cons: Large body, meh defense: large hurtbox means she's easily harassed by zoners, vulnerable to bigger combos, and can't backdash well; she's also slow, and her meterless reversal (623K) only shrinks her hurtbox instead of removing it
Poor ranged options: her longest normals (f.S, 2D, 6H) have poor follow-ups or are outright unsafe
Enemy option selects: her red-ball okizeme relies on a high/low mixup vulnerable to fuzzy guarding; opening up an opponent who understands how to negate her 5H can require specific callout options

uniqueMechanics.name: Delayed Gatlings
uniqueMechanics.description: Haehyun's gatlings are timed differently from other characters': instead of inputting the second attack just as the first is hitting, the second button should be slightly delayed until after the first makes contact and begins to recover. The timing is slightly more precise than traditional gatlings, but not difficult to use. Her aerial normals have normal gatling windows.

uniqueMechanics.name: Puppet Projectiles
uniqueMechanics.description: Her Tuning Ball projectiles (236S/236H) and Celestial Tuning Ball super (236236S) can be controlled independently of her body once active. Regular balls can be steered left and right; the super ball can also be steered up and down. The balls have momentum and are controlled with the stick, which also controls Haehyun herself, so proper ball control is needed for advanced okizeme and unblockable setups.

normalMoves.description: Useful as a quick anti-air/neutral check, for situations where c.S won't activate and her other anti-airs are too slow. Can't gatling into itself, so look elsewhere (2P) for abare. Situational, but good.
notes: On air hit, can gatling into 5K/c.S/5H/6H depending on range and height
On air counter hit, combos into red Shinken
Can stuff moves like Johnny's 6K

normalMoves.description: Essentially a mini f.S: slightly less range, but faster startup and more active frames. Good when approaching with 236S YRC, and can function as a niche anti-air. Has the most active frames of any of her grounded pokes.
notes: On air counter hit, can combo into red Shinken

normalMoves.description: Her go-to pressure normal/throw OS due to fast startup and frame advantage; a staple for continuing 236H okizeme. Gatlings into itself or 2D for easy ground combos or knockdowns. Can function as an anti-air but its short proximity range makes it unreliable unless the opponent is point blank (5P/6P are usually more reliable).
notes: On counter hit, links into 2H and gatling combos into 6P
6P gatling combos on crouching opponents, leading to Red Shinken loops

normalMoves.description: Her longest range normal footsie tool, though its lack of useful gatling options is a drawback. Generally canceled into 214K (Hayabusa) or blue ball (236S). Doesn't leave behind much hurtbox during recovery, making it notably difficult to whiff punish — but the long recovery still makes whiffing it a bad idea.

The overhead twin of 6K and one of her signature okizeme tools. The first hit has a lot of hitstop and a distinct animation, so aware opponents can stand and block the second hit if they block the first. To get the most as a mixup tool, use another normal to push the opponent out of the first hit's range, then try to connect only the second hit — usually done during H Tuning Ball oki, limiting counterattacks and enabling combos from 5H(2) into full Shinken loops. Against very aware opponents, canceling 5H(1) into the low 623[K] gives a moderate combo as a last resort. 5H(1) has some use in air combos from 6P since it's jump cancelable. Can technically anti-air, but other options are much better.
notes: Only the first hit is cancellable

normalMoves.description: Universal standing overhead that can also negate projectiles while the red glyph is present. One of the few 5Ds that's plus on block, though heavily telegraphed due to its distinct animation. Mediocre combos midscreen but great combos in the corner, including meterless unblockables with H Tuning Ball and 214[K]4 or meaty 5H overhead setups. Against cornered opponents, Hayabusa RRC > dash 5D6 is a scary threat converting minuscule damage and mediocre frame advantage into massive damage and oki. Can be YRC'd and turned into a mid-hitting projectile at the very end of its startup, creating visual noise and enabling tricks like pressing 5D again. Its projectile negation activates 1 frame faster than S Tuning Ball, recovers faster, and the attack itself isn't negated — but in practice it won't negate more than 2 hits, won't beat persistent/fullscreen projectiles (like Ky's Fortified Stun Edge), and rarely nets anything unless the opponent is immediately hit by 5D; IBing projectiles or staying evasive is usually the better response.

An anti-air with an odd mix of upper-body invuln and a few frames of high profile, since Haehyun lifts herself off the ground briefly during startup, letting her evade extremely low moves (e.g. Potemkin's Slidehead) though this is usually impractical. Because she crouches during startup, it can beat moves like Sin's Beak Driver, Faust's f.S and Scalpel Pull, and evade some projectiles — risky, but an option. Also a launcher that combos into red Shinken or 5H on normal hit; since it launches higher than 2H, using 6P instead of 2H to launch into Shinken loops is burst safe.
notes: Has a hitbox on both sides, useful against crossup moves (Elphelt/Millia rolls) and destroying Jack-O houses behind Haehyun

normalMoves.description: A slow, low-hitting move with a startup animation similar to 5H. Plus on block, but its primary use is as a mixup option supplementing 5H(2). Shorter range than 5H(2), so depending on hurtbox/position it may whiff where 5H(2) would hit.
notes: Staggers on normal hit

normalMoves.description: A high-risk, moderate-reward move. At a blistering 7F startup it can punish things outside the range of her other normals, especially after FD forces the opponent to whiff during a blockstring — though punishing this way sends the opponent nearly fullscreen, troublesome against characters who dominate her in neutral (Sin, Ky) or want to run away (Millia, Jack-O'). Counter hitting allows a combo, but she has safer ways to fish for counter hits; extremely situational due to a complete lack of cancel options making it extremely unsafe on block. Can be used as a gimmicky movement option when YRC'd.
notes: Knocks down and away on normal hit
Tumbles opponent on midscreen counter hit, wallbounces on corner counter hit
Midscreen counter hit can combo to 623[K]
Corner counter hit can combo to 2P

normalMoves.description: Her fastest normal and only ground normal that gatlings into itself. One of the best normals in the game for mashing due to its speed and range; also good for block punishing, especially after an IB. In combos, used for easier 2D confirms and continuing air combos on the ground (IAD combos, corner counter hit 6H, etc.).
notes: Her only true self-gatling that doesn't use the delay gatling system

normalMoves.description: A 6F low that gatlings into 2H to start Shinken loops; a fearsome mixup tool tempered by short range and 80% initial scaling. Also used to combo into 2D and as a low-pushback option for H Tuning Ball okizeme. Being plus on block is useful for frame trapping or conditioning. Has a very subtle animation and very little hitstop, making it too fast to react to in a blockstring.
Useful for pressuring opponents on okizeme and in blockstrings, and a decent low poke. Only combos into 214K from close range or on counter hit, but gatlings into 2D or f.S.

A meterless launcher and one of Haehyun's best combo starters because it reliably leads into Shinken loops. Both hits combo easily, even from 2K, and its fast startup makes it useful as a raw punish tool. Can be thrown out during a blockstring occasionally since either hit can be jump or special canceled for safety or a combo, and it builds good RISC. Her hurtbox lowers slightly during startup, and the second hit is an untechable knockdown on counter hit, giving it some anti-air utility — though using it that way without meter or a Tuning Ball to cover is a huge risk.
notes: Combos to red Shinken on normal hit

normalMoves.description: One of her longest range ground normals, though options out of it are mediocre special cancels (Hayabusa) or outright unsafe. Useful for securing knockdowns midscreen and in the corner, and can be gatlinged into from 2P, so it's not all bad — just don't use it as a poke. At certain ranges it may be her only meterless punish option for faraway moves like Ky's Stun Dipper or Greed Sever. Special canceling during recovery is useful for Tuning Balls: delay cancel into S ball YRC on block for a pressure re-buy, or into H ball on hit for her signature okizeme.
notes: Special cancelable during recovery
Moves Haehyun forward slightly
Pops up opponents enough to allow combos into blue Shinken if close enough, or even red Shinken with dash momentum

normalMoves.description: Her fastest and only self-gatling jump normal; the prime way to extend air combos, either into j.K for a jump cancel or j.H for a knockdown. Solid air-to-air due to its speed, upward hitbox, and self-gatling option, but don't expect a lot of damage.

A longer hitbox than j.P, but with no gatling options. Her only jump cancelable air normal, useful in combos. Combos to Falcon Dive (j.214K) on counter hit, getting a knockdown just enough to set up S Tuning Ball oki.

An unusual move with niche uses on grounded opponents, e.g. 2H > j.2K > crossup j.D. Its most relevant high-level usage is preventing opponents from getting in range to air throw at certain angles, or getting an unexpected hit during Danger Time.
notes: Pops Haehyun into the air on hit or block
After contact, she can steer herself forward and backward similar to Falcon Dive/Air Hayabusa
Can only be used once before returning to the ground

normalMoves.description: Has the most downward hitbox of her air normals, making it good for jump-ins or IADs, especially against crouching opponents. Short active frames and long recovery make it dangerous to whiff.

Her air blockstring and combo ender. Pretty large hitbox that reaches downward, able to stuff some 6Ps, but her linear air mobility and large hurtbox tarnish its use as an approach tool. When comboed into properly (around max normal jump height, while descending), it enables meaty H Tuning Ball okizeme.
notes: Knocks down from around the max height of a normal jump

normalMoves.description: Looks like a crossup and can hit as one, but can also hit from the front. Its wide hitbox helps it beat some 6Ps. Has use in IAD crossups, or combined with j.2K and/or air Hayabusa (j.214K).

universalMechanics.name: Ground Throw
universalMechanics.description: Grants universal H Tuning Ball okizeme midscreen. Haehyun can still control Tuning Balls during the throw animation, letting her combo off throw if a ball is active, making throws extremely rewarding for both starting and continuing offense. If RRC'd after throwing the opponent away from the nearest corner, she has enough time to charge and land red Hayabusa for easier, non-corner-specific damage. Since her 6H is extremely punishable whiffed/blocked, it's extremely important to option select her throw with c.S.

universalMechanics.name: Air Throw
universalMechanics.description: Grants universal H Tuning Ball okizeme midscreen. Though air throws are a universal anti-air option in Guilty Gear, her large aerial hurtbox, low aerial mobility, and lackluster j.P combos mean she takes more risk than average going for an air throw; since her CH anti-air confirms are more damaging, a grounded anti-air may be preferable unless absolutely necessary (e.g. versus Sol's Bandit Bringer and other disjointed, downward-reaching attacks).

universalMechanics.name: Dead Angle Attack
universalMechanics.description: Uses her 5K animation. Slow and punishable, but one of the more invincible Dead Angle Attacks, making it a viable defensive option.

universalMechanics.name: Blitz Attack
universalMechanics.description: Partial charge causes horizontal blowback on hit, wallsplats in the corner. Max charge (and counter hit partial charge) crumples on ground hit, floats and wall-sticks in the corner on air hit. Steals a small amount of Burst Gauge on hit. She generally doesn't need to gamble with Blitz since she has 2P and a reversal super, but a crumple enables red Shinken loops, tempting enough to consider occasionally.
notes: Proration: 55% (partial charge only)

specialMoves.name: Tuning Ball
specialMoves.description: A classic midrange space-control projectile with a twist: steerable left/right after leaving her hand. Disappears if Haehyun blocks, gets hit, gets rejected, or techs a throw. The S version is a steerable projectile that makes safer approaches versus characters without projectiles, and can make unsafe moves like 6H or 623[K] more palatable in neutral; long startup and the initial hitbox being slightly in front of Haehyun means an opponent can often jump over it, and it's very unsafe in blockstrings/stagger pressure unless YRC'd — sometimes used for okizeme when the H version would take too long. The H version (236H) is the linchpin of her okizeme: it forces the opponent to block one projectile hit, then the fireball floats behind them with two additional hits to strengthen pressure — safe pressure, combos from normal throw, and multiple 50/50 high/low mixups from a single knockdown with proper conditioning and ball control. When the H version isn't ready after a knockdown, she must choose between weaker S ball okizeme or YRCing an H ball.

specialMoves.name: Four Tigers Sword
specialMoves.input: 623K (hold OK): uncharged / partial charge (623[K]) / max charge

partialCharge.note: multiple short active phases while held (2-frame hits separated by ~6-frame gaps), final active phase 15F

maxCharge.note: multiple short active phases while held, longer charge than partial, final active phases around 6F and 3F

specialMoves.description: Uncharged (623K): a kick uppercut with upper-body invulnerability. Not a true invincible reversal since it only shrinks Haehyun's hurtbox rather than removing it (until the active frames). As an anti-air it's solid due to long active frames and high reach, even working against dive kicks like Elphelt's Air Bridal Express. On hit, RRC > 214[K] > red Shinken loops. Charged (623[K]): a high-risk, low-reward low-profile slide reminiscent of Grand Viper; its hurtbox isn't quite as low as Grand Viper so it clashes with some mid-hitting attacks instead of cleanly evading them. Carrying the opponent to the corner allows a combo with RC > 214[K] > red Shinken loops.

specialMoves.name: Four Tigers Sword (Reverse) / Shinken
specialMoves.description: Colloquially 'Shinken'. Normal version is blue, charged is red; attack connects 5F after K is released. The reason you play Haehyun: a high damage, normal-hit launcher that links into itself and can be comboed into from her primary mixup options, also letting her combo into a knockdown with j.H to set up more okizeme and repeat. Usually gets 2-3 red Shinkens from a simple 2K > 2H starter. Both versions wallbounce, but red has much more hitstun and can link into itself. Also functions as a slow but powerful anti-air (inheriting the startup upper-body invuln from 623[K]) and as a high-risk counterpoke, usually with 25 meter to YRC if the opponent doesn't bite. The blue version is usually done from a red Shinken or from 2D, enabling a short air combo into j.H to set up H Tuning Ball okizeme.
notes: Shi-shinken: the lenient transition from 623[K] to 623[K]4 allows canceling the first few active frames of 'Grandpa Viper' into Shinken, performed by holding 623[K] for a couple frames, releasing K, then tapping/holding 4K again; too quick a tap/hold cancels 623[K]'s startup before active frames, causing the first hit to seemingly whiff. Unlocks new corner conversions, mid-screen combo stabilization, and unique loops on some characters (notably Potemkin and Haehyun herself); can also be used mid-pressure/oki as a frame trap, YRC'd for safety, or combo'd into off a wakeup option
Above-knees invulnerability lasts as long as K is held
Changes to red version on frame 25
Cannot be held longer than 56F total
Can YRC at any point during startup or while K is held
Instant-release Shi-shinken has a 4-frame gap between the first and second hit, losing to multihits with a 3F gap or smaller on clash

specialMoves.name: Falcon Dive / Hayabusa
specialMoves.description: Colloquially 'hayabusa'. Normal version blue, charged red. Blue connects 6F after release, red connects 4F after. One of Haehyun's primary neutral tools since it hits airborne opponents and goes over lows; use it enough to make the opponent wary, but don't be predictable. Generally canceled into from f.S, which has no gatling options and isn't jump cancelable. Mostly safe on block due to pushback, but a well-timed IB can punish it — slightly delaying it can throw off IB timing. The red version is plus on block, a good way to re-buy pressure against a passive opponent. The blue version doesn't do much on normal hit, but on counter hit almost always links into 2D for decent okizeme; at close range against certain characters, a counterhit hayabusa even links to 2H for excellent damage. The red version wallbounces on air hit, leading to red Shinken loops or air combo options.
notes: Haehyun's hurtbox alters as she lifts her leg before the kick, letting the move go over low attacks if timed properly
Can inflict varying knockdown momentum on airborne opponents depending on which hitbox connects
-2 on normal block when spaced properly

specialMoves.name: Falcon Dive (Reverse)
specialMoves.description: Normal version blue, charged red; both connect quite a while after releasing K. A big overhead with big startup and big damage. Its very early frames look similar to the regular Hayabusa, making it slightly harder to react to than expected. A niche option in blockstrings to stay plus and build RISC, and can be used as a meaty against opponents with weak reversals/no meter for Blitz when Tuning Ball oki won't work. The red version can set up unblockables alongside her projectiles, forcing a stagger if blocked standing — unlike Leo or Johnny's forced staggers, the weak second hit will still knock the opponent down, preventing a free conversion without RC or a projectile to confirm into. Haehyun can use Celestial Tuning Ball super after a 5D6 corner combo to make the opponent sit still and convert from the second hit's small bounce.
notes: Both versions send the opponent at a sharp 40° curve upwards and wallbounce on hit
Her hurtbox shrinks as she lifts her leg and stays shrunk as long as K is held

specialMoves.name: Air Falcon Dive
specialMoves.description: Colloquially 'air hayabusa'. A steerable dive kick that supplements Haehyun's otherwise limited movement. Can bait anti-airs like any dive kick, but will often outright lose if the opponent doesn't take the bait. One of her only ways to maneuver while airborne, so it's worth using regularly. Can be comboed from on normal and counter hit; counter hit is generally easier and can allow a microdash into a ground combo or red Shinken loops.
notes: Spikes and groundbounces on hit, more so on counter hit

overdrives.name: Enlightened 3000 Palm Strike
overdrives.description: A 7F reversal super and combo tool. Not quite as unsafe as it looks since you can play a gimmicky game of chicken by moving the opponent around, but still very unsafe. A large circle appears around Haehyun while holding H/D; while the opponent is in the circle, they can be moved around with directional inputs. If done in a combo, the opponent is put into a capture state and can be freely moved around. Tumbles on hit, leading to combos in the corner or if hit behind Haehyun's back (opponent sent tumbling into her). Unblockable setups can start from corner 5D6 combos.
notes: Hyper armor while holding H, but throwable and vulnerable to supers
Unblockable after charging for 151 frames
Can hit slightly behind Haehyun

overdrives.name: Celestial Tuning Ball
overdrives.description: A 5-hit Tuning Ball, steerable up and down as well as left/right. A great okizeme tool for all the same reasons as H Tuning Ball, with more damage and hits. The projectile is large and obnoxious enough to help obscure what Haehyun is doing, especially something otherwise telegraphed like 5D. Slow to start up and maneuver, but builds decent speed once moving — a great way to steamroll neutral with enough meter and breathing room to set it up. Because it's a super, the opponent can't Burst out of it, useful at the end of a round to tack on more damage.
notes: Drastically reduced Tension gain while the ball is active
Stays onscreen even if Haehyun is hit; cannot be controlled while in hitstun or blockstun
Controllable up, down, left, and right once active
Player 1 ball is blue, Player 2 ball is orange/red

instantKill.name: Sundering Chord
instantKill.description: Haehyun generally has good ways to spend meter, especially given how combo-friendly her supers are. Her enormous damage output also means she doesn't really benefit from stockpiling meter and fishing for IK combos to end rounds.
notes: Uses the animation and hitbox of her 5D, but without the added effects
